name: Rikki Tikki Tavi
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (FS Road 7601 off Icicle Creek Road), follow the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599) to Colchuck Lake — 4 miles, 2,280 ft gain, a log-bridge crossing of Mountaineer Creek at 1.5 miles, staying right at the Lake Stuart Trail junction, finishing with a boulder-moraine climb to the outlet (2.5-3 hours, last reliable water). Continue toward the lake's south/east side onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail, gaining talus/heather to about 400 ft above the lake (30-40 min; holds wet snow into July, with a real slip-and-fall history), then cut climber's-left through dense slide-alder/heather brush (15-20 minutes) to the base gully below Colchuck Balanced Rock. Rikki Tikki Tavi (5.11, 5 pitches) sits to the right of The Scoop on the wall; expect loose 3rd/4th-class rock in the final scramble to the base. Total trailhead-to-base time is around 3.5-4 hours.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead (FR 7601)
waypoints.directions: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow it about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead. FR 7601 is gated closed from late fall through spring.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake outlet / north end
waypoints.directions: Hike the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles, and take the left fork onto the Colchuck Lake Trail at the junction. Climb the final boulder moraine to the lake's outlet at its north end, about 4 miles and 2,300 ft from the car. Fill water here.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Balanced Rock summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the trail counter-clockwise around the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. At about 400 ft above the lake, cut climber's left through dense slide alder and heather into the gully below the west face and scramble loose 3rd and 4th class ground to the base, then climb the route's five pitches to the summit ridge.
